change.title: npm @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default; MessageParam becomes a union, temperature/top_p/top_k removed, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry SDKs must move to v1 too

source.quote: * **api:** add support for new API version 2026-10-21

tasks.reasoning:
The repo pins @anthropic-ai/sdk ^0.20.0. A caret range on 0.x stays below 0.21.0, so nothing changes automatically and nothing breaks today. The 1.0.0 major covers every version below 1.0.0, so this is a planned upgrade task, not an emergency. The one call site (ai.js:32) sends model claude-sonnet-4-20250514, max_tokens, system and messages, and none of these is removed in API version 2026-10-21. The jump is large (0.20 to 1.0), so the migration agent should check: client construction, how the response is read (content blocks, error classes, streaming helpers changed across 0.x releases), and that historyMessages entries still fit the new MessageParam union. It should also confirm no sampling params or document/citation blocks are ever added, and opt out of OpenTelemetry if the app has a global tracer provider. Low urgency: no deadline, and the old SDK keeps working with 2023-06-01.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- anthropic:2026-10-21-api-version-2026-10-21 (api-version): New Claude API version 2026-10-21 (anthropic-version header); SDKs older than the new majors keep sending 2023-06-01. SDK 1.0.0 sends anthropic-version 2026-10-21 by default. The repo's ^0.20.0 SDK keeps sending 2023-06-01, so the API-version move happens through this SDK upgrade. The single messages.create call (model, max_tokens, system, messages) uses nothing the new version removes.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "This guide lists the code changes for moving from API version `2023-06-01` to `2026-10-21`."
- anthropic:2026-10-14-ts-sdk-otel-default (other): TypeScript SDK 0.134.0 auto-creates OpenTelemetry spans and trace headers if a global tracer provider exists (unsure if affects; opt out with openTelemetry:false). OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation arrives in SDK 0.134.0, which this repo only reaches by upgrading. During the bump the agent should check whether the app registers a global tracer provider and, if needed, pass openTelemetry:false.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "If your app registers a global tracer provider, the SDK will create spans with it after upgrading, and they'll be exported with the rest of your traces."

callSites.why: anthropic.messages.create is built from @anthropic-ai/sdk ^0.20.0. Moving to 1.0.0 changes the default API version to 2026-10-21 and makes MessageParam a union type. The call passes model, max_tokens, system and historyMessages and no temperature, top_p or top_k, so the request body itself should stay valid.

record.prBody:
## npm @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default; MessageParam becomes a union, temperature/top_p/top_k removed, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry SDKs must move to v1 too [Verified]

### Change

Bumped @anthropic-ai/sdk ^0.20.0 to 1.0.0 via npm. ai.js now joins text blocks instead of reading content[0].text. Added test/ai.check.js (mocked fetch): checks the returned text, that no temperature/top_p/top_k is sent, that anthropic-version is 2026-10-21, and that SDK is 1.x. The app has no tracer provider, so openTelemetry is left at its default. No Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry usage. History messages are only user/assistant turns, so the MessageParam union is fine. No sampling params, documents or citations are used. License of SDK changes MIT to Apache-2.0.

Files touched:
- `ai.js`
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `test/ai.check.js`

### Why

1.0.0 defaults to API version 2026-10-21 and makes ContentBlock/MessageParam unions, so content[0].text needs narrowing.

> * **api:** add support for new API version 2026-10-21

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ai-check | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- ai-check, added by the agent: `node test/ai.check.js` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Prepared before the baseline:
- Preparation changed repo files, kept out of this PR: package-lock.json.

Test of this change: `ai-check`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Real API behaviour at 2026-10-21 and model id claude-sonnet-4-20250514 availability
- No type check exists (plain JS)
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- Reply text is now the concatenation of all text blocks rather than only the first block
- Requests now send anthropic-version 2026-10-21

---

preparation.reasoning: No setup steps are needed. The package.json has only start and dev scripts, with no build, codegen, postinstall or prepare step. There are no workspace packages or subfolder projects to install, and no checks were detected. The env vars in .env.example (Twilio and Anthropic keys) are only read at runtime, so nothing needs them just to load or build.

review.summary: The only call site (ai.js:32) sends no temperature, top_p or top_k, so the removed parameters need no change. The SDK bump in package.json and the lockfile is consistent. The ai.js change from `content[0].text` to joining every text block is a sensible guard now that responses may contain non-text or multiple blocks. The new check stubs fetch and confirms three things: the 2026-10-21 version header, that sampling parameters are absent, and that the installed SDK is 1.x. It never makes a live call, so it does not prove the model id or real transport work under SDK 1.0 and the new API version. I could not confirm the SDK 1.0 details (Node requirement, MessageParam union shape) from memory; they should be checked against the CHANGELOG and the SDK's types. The verified grade is reasonable for a stubbed check, with those limits.

concerns.issue: Behaviour change beyond the API change: if the response has no text blocks (empty content, or only non-text blocks), askJasmin now returns '' instead of throwing. The caller (index.js, not shown) may then send an empty WhatsApp reply through Twilio instead of hitting its error path.

The lockfile drops node-fetch, agentkeepalive and the polyfills, so SDK 1.0 appears to rely on the runtime's native fetch. package.json has no `engines` field, so if production runs an old Node version the client could fail at runtime. The check stubs globalThis.fetch, so it would not catch this. Confirm the SDK's Node requirement and the deploy Node version.

The model 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514' is unchanged and is never exercised against the real API under version 2026-10-21; the check returns a canned response. I could not confirm the model is still accepted under this version; check Anthropic's model and deprecation docs.
The check is not wired into package.json scripts (there is no `test` script), so CI may not run it. It also tests only one history shape (a single assistant turn, then the user turn).

Not shown. If it catches SDK errors (e.g. Anthropic.APIError, status codes) or imports anything else from @anthropic-ai/sdk, the 1.0 major bump may have renamed or moved those exports. Only ai.js was named as a call site.

checkFirst: Make one real call to askJasmin with the 1.0 SDK in the production Node version, to confirm transport, model id and the API version header end to end.
Check the deployed Node version against SDK 1.0's minimum, given that node-fetch was removed.
Grep index.js and other files for other @anthropic-ai/sdk imports or error-class handling.
Decide whether an empty string from askJasmin should be treated as an error before replying through Twilio.
